 Order
Per: Justice Vivek Rusia Heard on the question of admission.

The petitioners have filed the present petition, being aggrieved by the order dated 02.5.2025 passed by the Central Administrative Tribunal (for short the "Tribunal") in Original Application No.
200/569/2023 whereby the Tribunal has dismissed the Original Applications.
2. Facts of the case, in short, are as under:-
The petitioner No.1 owned a land bearing Survey No.43, situated in the village Rerua Kala, Tahsil Nagod, District Satna.

Petitioner No.2 owned a land bearing Survey No.128/2 situated at village Nunahi, Tahsil Devendra Nagar, District Panna and Petitioner No.3 owned land bearing Survey NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:279 2 MP-6992-2025 No.1/1/1 Min./4 situated in village Badira Bumari, Tahsil Devendra Nagar, District Panna.

entities.text: 0.35 Manoj Kumar Mishra vs Union Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2. It is not in dispute that upon acquisition of lands amount of compensation of Rs.11,70,147/-,
Rs.61,096.35 P & Rs.2,34,531/- were duly paid to the petitioners under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement Act, 2013 vide Awards dated 27.6.2017, 28.7.2017 & 10.11.2017 respectively.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Pursuant to the notification dated 14.10.2016, the petitioners submitted applications for the grant of employment in the Railways.

Initially, their applications were processed but later on the Railway Board vide circular dated 11.11.2019 No.E(NG)II/2010/RC-5/1 withdrawn the policy for grant of employment in lieu of acquisition of the land and made provisions for payment of compensation of Rs.5 lacs in lieu of acquired land if certificate is given by the Collector under sections 31(1), 38(1) &
105(3) of the aforesaid Act of 2013 to the effect that family was dependent from the earnings of land acquired.

Meaning thereby, at the time of consideration of their applications, there was no such policy for the grant of employment; therefore, vide order dated 22.12.2022, the Senior Divisional Personnel Officer, West Central Railway, Jabalpur, rejected the claim of the petitioners NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:279 3 MP-6992-2025 for the grant of employment.
Apart from the aforesaid ground, the petitioners were found over-age as on 01.1.2017.

Most importantly, the acquired land was very less, from which earnings were not sufficient to earn a livelihood for the entire family; therefore, there was no loss to the petitioners in respect of earnings from the land area acquired for the construction of the railway line.
Thus, the petitioners were not found entitled to a rehabilitation appointment under the aforesaid Rehabilitation Policy.
All the petitioners filed Original Applications, which were dismissed by the impugned order dated 02.5.2025.

4. Without disputing the facts mentioned therein i.e. age, less area of land, age bar, dependency on the earnings of a small piece of land, the petitioners have come up with a plea that certain similarly placed persons have been granted employment by relaxing the age criteria.
5. It is the prerogative of the respondents to grant relaxation or not for the grant of compassionate appointment in addition to the monetary compensation.
No writ can be issued by the High Court in the absence of any policy available in the respondent's establishment.
There cannot be negative parity.
Under what circumstances the relaxation of age was given to others has not been brought to record.
There is no dispute to the fact that, as of today, no policy for the grant of employment is available in the Railways.
The area of the acquired land was also very less to claim that livelihood has gone due to the acquisition of the land for the railway project.

Therefore, no writ can be issued to the respondents, and the petitioners are not entitled to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:279 4 MP-6992-2025 any relief.
6. In the result, no interference with the order dated 02.5.2025 passed by the "Tribunal" in Original Application No. 200/569/2023 , hence the petition stands dismissed.
